Tasktypes.explorationDescription: The player explores the environment for a set duration without a destination flag. The next task starts automatically when time runs out.
Tasktypes.navigationtasksDescription: Navigation tasks direct the player to new locations.
Tasktypes.thematictasksDescription: Thematic tasks are location-specific tasks with different thematic content.
Tasktypes.informationDescription: The 'information' module can be used to give the player hints and tips.
Tasktypes.navtoflagDescription: In navigation-to-a-flag tasks, the player sees a flag on the map that marks a destination. His/her job is to go to this place.
Tasktypes.navwitharrowDescription: Navigation-with-arrow is a navigation with arrow and distance information, which shows the player the direction to the next destination. The map is not visible.
Tasktypes.navviatextDescription: In a navigation-via-text task, the player receives precise navigation instructions to the next destination.
Tasktypes.navviaphotoDescription: The task type navigation-via-photo navigates the player to the next destination using a photo.
Tasktypes.selflocDescription: With self-location tasks the player has to find his/her current location on the map.
Tasktypes.objectlocDescription: The object-location task type includes the assignment of objects on the map to objects in the environment and vice versa.
Tasktypes.directiondetermDescription: In direction-determination tasks, the player must relate his view-direction with the map alignment.
Tasktypes.freetasksDescription: In free tasks, question and answer types of the task can be freely combined. In this way, for example, quizzes and thematic tasks can be asked.

content.0: In GeoGami you can play games created by yourself or by others. To see a list of games, choose 'Games' from the main menu, or scan a QR code if you have one.

content.0: Zoom: choose whether the zoom should be set to the task, to the game, by the player, or not at all.
content.1: Map section: choose whether the entire map section or a specific one is always visible, or whether the map section moves along with the player and can therefore shift.
content.2: Map rotation: set the orientation of the map (does the player always look up, or is north always at the top?)
content.3: Position marker: the position-marker setting changes the task significantly. If turned off, players have to orient themselves only by their surroundings to decide where they are. If turned on, they can orient themselves by the marker. If turned on only at the start of the task, they can orient themselves once at the start; if on demand, they can decide themselves how often they need this hint.
content.4: View-direction marker: the same notes apply as for the position marker. In addition, this marker shows not only the location but also the direction the player is facing. This feature only works if the position marker is enabled.
content.5: Track recording: when you enable track recording, players can see and follow their own movement live on the map. Children enjoy 'drawing' shapes like circles or hearts on the map. Track recording only refers to visualising on the map — in the background GeoGami always records the track.
content.6: Street highlighting: you can highlight the street section the player is currently on in red. Unlike the position marker, this does not reveal the exact position.
content.7: Highlight landmarks: use this to point out things in the landscape that, for example, can make orientation easier.

content.0:
Depending on the task type, you can configure further settings that improve the play experience or better address the goal of the task.
Enable or disable input confirmation: this controls whether players themselves have to confirm that they solved the task correctly.
content.1: Show flag: this sets the difficulty of the task by determining whether the destination flag is visible on the map.
content.2: Enable or disable feedback: this determines whether players immediately learn whether they solved the task correctly.
content.3: Keep flag on the map: this determines whether the destination of this task remains visible during the next tasks.
content.4: Enable multiple attempts: this determines whether players get a new chance if they solve the task incorrectly (only for thematic tasks).
content.5: Accuracy: set how close to the destination players must be to be considered 'in the right place'. Due to GPS inaccuracies, do not choose too small a distance.
content.6: Under Map features you can configure further settings for the position marker and for interaction with the map itself. These can be tried out under 'Learn' in the main menu.
content.7: Highlight landmarks: use this to point out things in the landscape that, for example, can make orientation easier.

mapType.label: Map type
mapType.description: Which kind of map players see, for example standard or satellite.

mapSwitchLayer.label: Switch to satellite layer
mapSwitchLayer.description: Lets players of a virtual world switch the map to its satellite view. Only offered for virtual worlds that have a satellite layer.

mapLocationMarker.label: Location marker
mapLocationMarker.description: Shows the player’s own position on the map.

mapDirectionMarker.label: View direction marker
mapDirectionMarker.description: Shows the direction the player is looking in.

mapTrack.label: Track recording
mapTrack.description: Shows the walked track on the map during the game, together with the option for how long it stays on the map.

mapStreetHighlight.label: Highlight street section at location
mapStreetHighlight.description: Highlights the street section at the player’s position.

mapLocationBuffer.label: Map section (buffer) at location
mapLocationBuffer.description: Limits the visible map to a circle around the player, together with the diameter of that circle.

mapLandmarks.label: Highlighting of landmarks
mapLandmarks.description: Highlights landmarks on the map, together with the landmark drawing.

virtualEnvironmentChoice.label: Choose a virtual world
virtualEnvironmentChoice.description: Selects the virtual world a task takes place in.

virtualTaskFloor.label: Task floor
virtualTaskFloor.description: The floor a task takes place on in building worlds. Needed for those worlds.

virtualInitialPose.label: Avatar start position and direction
virtualInitialPose.description: Sets where the avatar starts and which way it faces, including the start floor in buildings. Without it the existing default start is used.

virtualCameraClip.label: Camera clipping distance
virtualCameraClip.description: Limits how far the camera sees.

virtualEnvironmentSettings.label: Show environment settings
virtualEnvironmentSettings.description: Shows the environment settings to players.

virtualPathVisualization.label: Show path visualization
virtualPathVisualization.description: Shows the path in building worlds.

virtualMapSize.label: Map size
virtualMapSize.description: How large the map is shown in the virtual world.

virtualLandmarkSelection.label: Landmarks to show
virtualLandmarkSelection.description: Chooses which landmarks of the virtual world are visible.

editorModeSwitch.label: Simple / Advanced switch
editorModeSwitch.description: The switch itself. It is always available to everyone who can open an editor.

taskInstruction.label: Task instruction and audio message
taskInstruction.description: What players are asked to do. Needed for every task.

taskDestination.label: Destination and reference inputs
taskDestination.description: Inputs the selected task type needs, such as the destination or a reference direction.

taskExplorationSettings.label: Exploration duration and timer
taskExplorationSettings.description: Duration and timer of an exploration task. Needed for that task type.

taskCollaborationMethod.label: Collaboration method (multiplayer)
taskCollaborationMethod.description: How the players of a multiplayer task share instructions. Needed for multiplayer tasks.

taskConfirmation.label: Input confirmation
taskConfirmation.description: Asks players to confirm their input (navigation to a flag or via text).

taskFeedback.label: Feedback
taskFeedback.description: Shows players feedback on their answer.

taskAutoPlayAudio.label: Play audio automatically
taskAutoPlayAudio.description: Plays a task’s audio message automatically. Also in information tasks.
